mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals a contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained INDPRO contraction (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the federal funds rate below 2% coincident with a rise in real savings (RSAFS) signals a liquidity injection and risk-on environment, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change < -0.75% AND RSAFS monthly change > 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, boosting consumer demand and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 200000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained strong PAYEMS growth (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based demand contraction, which reduces corporate revenue and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -0.3% AND HOUST monthly change < -2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 4% for six consecutive months, coupled with a federal funds rate below 3%, signals a persistent inflation surprise in a low-rate environment, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 104 for 6 consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 3%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of high inflation and low rates (t-test p > 0.05).
